subject: Renewal: buffer-pool allocation & committed GPU add for Q3
messages:

Cc: Roger Tan <roger.tan@sentinel.ai>, procurement@sentinel.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — buffer pool question and usage file attached

Hi Jasmine,

As we approach our annual renewal, procurement asked me to get a clear recommendation from Redwood on how to avoid the mid-quarter throttles we've had the last two months. We've attached our April usage slice so you can see the short spikes.

Quick context: we're currently on a 120-GPU committed pool with burst enabled. Last three months show average utilization at ~68% but short bursts hit 92–96% for 5–12 minute windows. That’s what triggered the throttles.

Can Redwood provide: 1) an option to add committed GPUs to smooth these spikes, 2) an alternative buffer pool approach (temporary reserved buffer), and 3) an estimated cost delta for each option?

We're aiming to finalize commitment changes by end of month so procurement can sign the amendment before May billing.

Thanks — attaching the usage CSV (usage_report_apr2027.csv).

— Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Sentinel AI

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — buffer pool question and usage file attached

Hi Elena — thanks for the data, that helps. I pulled the April slice and ran it through our transient-burst model. High level takeaways:

- Current committed: 120 GPUs.
- Median sustained utilization: 68%.
- Peak transient windows (5–12 min): 92–96% — these are the throttle triggers.

Three practical options for Sentinel (sorted by reliability -> cost):

1) Add committed GPUs (steady-state): +12 GPUs to committed pool (to 132) — smooths peaks and reduces throttles across 99th percentile windows. Estimated incremental cost: +14% monthly on committed invoice vs current.

2) Dedicated buffer pool (short-term reserved): create a 16-GPU buffer reserve that is reserved but billed at a reduced buffer rate for 12 months; automatic pull-in when bursts exceed 90%. Less cost than fully committed but still guaranteed.

3) Burst smoothing + caching tweaks (no commit): optimize KV prefix caching and enable auto-prefetch for predictable jobs; combined with a 4–8 GPU burst reservation gives a cheaper, lower-latency fix but still risks rare throttles during long sustained surges.

Recommendation: given your burst profile and Q3 product roadmap, option 1 (add +12 committed) gives the cleanest SLA improvement. Option 2 is a good compromise if you want capacity guarantees without full committed pricing.

I'm attaching a brief proposal with estimated costs and a sample amendment language for both options (proposed_buffer_amendment_v1.pdf).

Next steps: if you want to proceed we can draft the amendment and Vanessa can confirm pricing/crediting. Happy to set a 30-minute call this week to walk the numbers.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed_buffer_amendment_v1.pdf]

Elena — quick pricing note from finance side. We can offer the following commercial accommodations if Sentinel signs a 12-month addendum by 31 May:

- Option A (Committed +12 GPUs): 6% consumption credit on the incremental committed capacity for the first 3 months.
- Option B (16-GPU buffer reserve): buffer resources billed at the buffer reserve rate (approx. 25% discount vs on-demand) + waived one-time amendment processing fee.

Operational note: We'll need a signed amendment and at least 6 weeks lead time to reserve ledgers for tranche provisioning if you choose committed capacity. If you need faster turn-up we can support staged provisioning with partial burst until full tranches are online.

I'll align the amendment language with Jasmine and route to contracts.

— Vanessa Ortiz

Looping in a quick operational reality check: provisioning lead time for committed tranches is currently ~6 weeks from signed amendment to active (this includes procurement of reserved capacity and orchestration windows). Q3 hardware forecast looks tight in weeks 27–31, so if Sentinel wants a full committed +12 by start of Q3, we need the signed amendment no later than 31 May. Otherwise, we can do a hybrid: stage 6 GPUs immediately (2-week lead via burst-to-reserve swap) and pull the rest once capacity is available.

Also, recommend we include an automated fallback policy in the amendment: when committed pool is offline or constrained, route to compatible hosted instances with a defined cost uplift. That will reduce customer impact during provisioning windows.

Ben Carter
Renewals Ops
Redwood Inference
